newsitem.title: FINLAND: VIKING LINE BUYS FERRY FOR FIM 470 MLN.
newsitem.headline: VIKING LINE BUYS FERRY FOR FIM 470 MLN.

text.p: Finnish passenger ferry operator Viking Line Ab has bought ferry Silja Scandinavia from Swedish Sea Ling Shipping AB in a deal worth a total of 470 million markka including new investments, Viking said in a statement.
"The value of the ship acquisition including supplementary investments is about 470 million markka," Viking said.

Currently, Silja Scandinavia is chartered out to Silja Line, part of Silja Oy , which is Viking Line's biggest competitor in passenger ferry traffic between Finland and Sweden, Viking said, adding it would receive the ferry in April 1997.
Silja Scandinavia was built in 1992. Its passenger capacity is 2,400, it has 678 cabins with 2,128 beds and space for 400 private cars or 50 lorries.
The ferry would replace one of Viking Line's current ferries in regular traffic between Finland and Sweden, Viking said, but did not specify which one.
After taking the now purchased ferry into use, Viking said the average age of its fleet would be 5-1/2 years lower than "the ships in Baltic Sea traffic owned by the biggest competitor."
